sampling_unit: participant: one AI participant per original human participant; n is participants per arm

agents.role: decision-maker who reads the vignette and answers (original human participants in Studies 1 and 2)

arms.description: Each AI participant answers all 13 moral dilemmas in one session, in a random order, seeing the earlier vignettes and its own earlier answers.
Original framing; each AI participant answers one of the six dilemmas.

order.s1: vignette order randomised per participant (seeded); block order not replayed (only moral dilemmas)
order.s2: one vignette per participant; vignettes assigned in a seeded, balanced shuffle

visibility.s1: earlier vignettes and the participant's own answers in this run

assignment: Within each arm the six Study 2 dilemmas are assigned in a balanced, seeded shuffle (between-subjects).
replay_adaptations: The participant instruction is the SI S4.1 participant prompt (the human instruction text is not printed); the sentence "You will be shown a total of 13 scenarios" is kept unchanged in both studies.
Human response format is not printed; the AI participant answers yes or no after the appended instruction "Please answer only with yes or no."
In Study 1 the session text lists earlier vignettes with the participant's own answers ("Your answer: ...") to carry what a person remembers; this scaffolding is not from the paper.
not_replayed: Study 1 collective action problems (vignettes and slider ranges not available)
Study 4 (the subjects are specific models; no human participants)
LLM arms, advice/expert/silicon prompts and the human-versus-LLM ANOVAs
